messages:
luna: Heads-up: gpux-pool-4 showing heavy GPU host paging and a flurry of nccl errors in logs. Latency for text.generate jumped 6-8x around 21:12 UTC. KV cache memory usage went from ~22% -> 92% in ~90s. Paging to host swap observed. Paging + NCCL = bad. Paging alert: paging.gpu.high.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED 1310000000 id=INC-2023100 severity=high. Triggers: gpu_paging > 2, kv_cache_usage > 90% for 2m, nccl_timeout_count > 50. Runbook: /runbooks/kv-cache-paging + oncall.

marco: I'm on call. Quick scan: continuous-batching window suddenly increased for many requests (auto-window growth logic to maximize throughput hit a pathological case). That resulted in very large KV prefix caches for a subset of tensor-parallel shards. One TV shard reached ~152MB while peers were ~28-36MB. NCCL allreduce sizes diverged and rings started timing out at step boundaries.

jess: Confirmed on logs: repeated messages like: "nccl: Allreduce timed out after 60s" and "kv_shard_manager: shard_size_exceeded_hint: 152MB". We also saw an influx of long-prefix requests from a single customer token bucket.

sre-oncall: Taking ownership. Immediate mitigations proposal (live): 1) globally cap continuous-batching window to 64 2) set KV_SHARD_HARD_LIMIT=80MB 3) pause routing to gpux-pool-4 for new sessions (drain gracefully) 4) extend NCCL timeout temporarily to avoid cascading deadlocks. Any other quick wins?

rao: Agreed. Also recommend enabling the runtime's "batch formation reject" circuit-breaker to refuse batches that would cause projected shard delta > 32MB. I'll craft a live override.

cs-oncall: Customer impact: from CS dashboard quick view, five tenants hit errors (streaming disconnects & 502/504) since 21:11-21:15 UTC. Opening support tickets and holding a short customer note.

luna: Do the live changes. Please paste commands when you run them.

marco: Running live config overrides now. Patch applied to configmap and adding an env var for the runtime pods so rollout is controlled. Commands:

```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"CONTINUOUS_BATCH_MAX":"64","KV_SHARD_HARD_LIMIT":"83886080","NCCL_TIMEOUT_MS":"180000"}}'
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/runtime --selector=pool=gpux-pool-4 --timeout=10m
```

deploy-bot: Configmap runtime-config patched by marco. Rolling restart initiated for deployments with selector pool=gpux-pool-4.

jess: Also pushed a small change to the runtime to enable the batch-formation circuit-breaker gate (flag only): set via env in deployment until PR merges.

```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runtime BATCH_DELTA_REJECT=enabled
```

marco: We've enabled the reject gate; new batch formation logs show rejections for some oversized batches (e.g., "batch-reject: projected_shard_delta=47MB"). That prevented further shard growth.

rao: Observability: increased kv-shard-manager log level and enabled per-pod token-level tracing for the affected deploys. I've started a live dashboard for shard size distribution.

luna: Any sign of recovery?

jess: After the rollout: KV shard sizes rebalanced to ~30-50MB across TP ranks within ~3 minutes. NCCL timeouts dropped to baseline. Paging stopped on hosts in gpux-pool-4. Error rate for text.generate is back down to near-normal.

cs-oncall: Notifying impacted customers that we've mitigated and are working on root cause + postmortem. Some clients saw up to 30% failed requests during the window.

marco: Root cause hypothesis: a recent ML model tweak increased average prefix token variance for a small traffic slice; combined with an aggressive continuous-batching auto-scaling heuristic that prioritizes batch width over shard balance, we ended up with highly asymmetric KV shards under tensor-parallel distribution. Runtime lacked a hard upper bound on per-shard cache growth.

rao: Fixes we need to ship: 1) permanent circuit-breaker at batch formation to consider projected shard delta 2) enforce KV_SHARD_HARD_LIMIT in kv-shard-manager with eviction policy 3) make continuous-batching heuristic shard-aware (bias against creating wide batches if projected shard imbalance > threshold) 4) add unit/integration tests that simulate long-prefix skew and ensure no shard > 80MB.

luna: Who's owning the postmortem and code changes?

marco: I'll own the ops-runbook updates and the quick hotfix PR for the batch reject gate. rao will own kv-shard-manager hard-limit + tests. jess will add the continuous-batching heuristic change in the serving runtime repo. cs-oncall will handle customer comms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE id=INC-2023100 status=mitigated mitigation=runtime-config-cap, batch-reject enabled, draining gpux-pool-4

marco: Quick note for the postmortem: collect: 1) config diffs (kubectl get configmap runtime-config -o yaml) 2) pod logs for kv-shard-manager and nccl 3) traffic histogram showing prefix length distribution for 60m before incident 4) stack traces for any runtimes that hit the reject gate.

jess: Also scheduling a canary rollout of the batching-heuristic change in staging with synthetic long-prefix traffic to validate.

luna: Handoff: I'm handing this over to marco for follow-ups and RCA. If anything degrades overnight page sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll standby for paging alerts and coordinate if we need oncall escalation.

marco: Final admin: drafting postmortem and will aim to have a draft within 72 hours. CS will prepare customer impact details for SLA ops.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED id=INC-2023100 resolved_at=2310000090 root_cause_tag=kv-shard-imbalance-continuous-batching mitigation_summary=cap-and-reject-batches

cs-oncall: Added customer impact table to the incident doc and requested credit review for impacted tenants.

luna: Thanks team. Closing after postmortem posted. :thumbsup:
